title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a recapitulative theorem in Grothendieck's combinatorial 'analysis situs' of a one-dimensional totally ordered model L or M (a 'line'). The objects are figures, préfigures and polygones, meaning finite unions of points and intervals.

Notation from the previous page:
- A flag D ∈ Drap*(L) is a finite non-empty chain of points of L.
- ∂D is empty if card D = 1, and {inf D, sup D} if card D ≥ 2.
- F_D is the closed figure (the closed segment from inf D to sup D, stratified by the points of D).
- For α ⊂ ∂D, Φ_{D,α} = F_D \ α.
- Part 1 of the theorem: (D, α) ↦ Φ_{D,α} is a bijection onto the connected common préfigures, i.e. intervals with some endpoints removed.
- Part 2: Φ is closed iff α = ∅.

Openness criterion (top of this page). Let Θ be the set of extreme elements of L (its least and/or greatest element, if they exist), so card Θ ∈ {0, 1, 2}. Then Φ is open iff card D ≥ 2 and α = ∂D − (∂D ∩ Θ). In words, the interval must be non-degenerate and open at each endpoint, except at an endpoint that is an extremity of L, where a closed end is open in L. The machine transcription reads 'connexe' here, but the context (previous page: 'Pour que Φ soit ouverte, il faut et suffit…') makes it the openness criterion.

Part 3. Consider a chain D = {Φ1 <! Φ2 <! … <! Φn} of connected polygons. The relation Φ <! Ψ means Φ lies strictly before Ψ and Φ ∪ Ψ is not connected; the previous page characterises non-connectedness of Φ ∪ Ψ by Φ <! Ψ or Ψ <! Φ. Set Φ_D = ⋃_i Φ_i. This is a disjoint union, it is a polygon, and its connected components are exactly the Φ_i. The map D ↦ Φ_D from Dr*_{<!}(Polygconn(M)) to Polyg(M) is a bijection. In other words, every polygon of a line decomposes uniquely as a finite ordered family of pairwise separated connected pieces.

Part 4 (continued on the next page). Φ_D is closed (respectively open) iff each component is.

The next page then turns to computing the 'rapports' of a polygon, additively over its connected components. Overall, this is the one-dimensional base case of a combinatorial theory of tame stratified spaces.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. The openness criterion is correct, including the subtlety that endpoints of L belonging to the interval do not obstruct openness.

On 'D ∈ Drap*(L)': in the previous page's formulation the bijection is only meaningful if D is understood as the set of vertices relevant to the interval (or only via inf/sup). Several D give the same underlying set unless F_D carries its stratification. This is a matter of conventions, not an error.

ideas.what: Classification of connected definable subsets (préfigures) of a totally ordered 'line' as intervals given by a flag of points plus a set of removed endpoints.
ideas.modern_name: Cell decomposition in dimension 1 / intervals in a dense linear order (o-minimal monotonicity setup)
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic call for 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the detailed Analysis situs notes are unpublished.

ideas.what: Openness criterion for an interval, involving the set Θ of extreme points of L.
ideas.modern_name: Order topology: half-open intervals at the ends of the order are open

ideas.what: Unique decomposition of a polygon (finite union of cells) into a strictly separated chain of connected components; closedness and openness tested componentwise.
ideas.modern_name: Connected components of definable sets in dimension 1

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but elementary bookkeeping of one-dimensional tame topology: intervals, their openness and closedness, and connected components. It is interesting only as part of Grothendieck's unpublished combinatorial 'analysis situs', which ran parallel to o-minimality. It contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Alors Φ est connexe ssi' should almost certainly read 'Alors Φ est ouverte ssi'. This is the openness criterion announced on the previous page.
'soit Θ l'image … la partie de L, des cardinal {0,1,2}, … densité … élément' is better read as 'soit Θ l'ensemble … la partie de L, de cardinal ∈ {0,1,2}, formée de ses éléments extrémaux'.
'dans 𝒞 un ordinal des … polygones' is likely 'dans l'ens. ordonné des (pré)polygones connexes'.
In D = {Φ1 ≤! Φ2 <! …}, the first relation is presumably also <! (strict separation).
The struck words at the start of item 3 should be read as a deleted 'connexes' near the chain and a deleted 'suite de polygones'.
